characters: Little Hen: a small round brown hen with a red comb and bright round eyes.
Goat: a cheerful brown goat with a white nose.
Dog: a floppy-eared tan dog with a wagging tail.
Duck: a white duck with an orange beak.
Pipi: a tiny yellow chick who looks closely at everything.

narrationPlan.voice: Funny, expressive voice with different animal sounds
narrationPlan.pace: Slow, with repeated lines and big sneezes (about 85 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: Light bouncy pizzicato with comic slide whistle (placeholder)
culturalNotes: A farmyard scene typical of many Ghanaian homes; no cultural claims are made.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Are the animal sounds and repeated lines suitable for read-aloud with 3–4 year-olds?

teacherGuide.overview: A cause-and-effect chain with a joyful repeated sneeze. A very small character solves the problem by looking closely.
learningGoals: Retell a chain of events in order.
Hear /d/ at the start of words.
whileReading: Invite children to say “Atchoo!” on cue.
Ask what might happen next before each page turn.
afterReading: Act out the chain, each child choosing an animal.
discussion: How did Pipi know what was wrong?
reflection: What small thing have you noticed that a bigger person missed?

support: Point to each animal as it is named.
stretch: Add a new animal to the chain.
